chapter: Boston roadhouses and the Army band
title: The 807th Pioneer band, Junkman Rag and not Jim Europe's 369th
summary: They play Lucky Roberts's 'Junkman Rag' for the president of France; Whaley clarifies he was in the 807th Pioneer regiment, not Jim Europe's 369th, and mentions a captain who resigned.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: we went to entertain President ______, he was the president at the time and when he got off the train the band played the 'Junkman Rag,' Lucky Roberts' 'Junkman Rag.'
Lucky Roberts was a piano player here in New York, wasn't he, and a great composer, too.
Right, and we played the 'Junkman Rag' for President ______, president of France.
And this band was called a pioneer --
We got to talk about Will Vodrey a little later on, because he's another one of the greats like you.
I am going to tell you about -- you remember when he was down at the Cotton Club.
Yes, sir. We will talk about that, we don't want to forget about Vodrey.
Now this band wasn't called the 369th band was it.
No, that was Jim Europe. That was Jim Europe had the 369th.
You were in the Pioneer what.
I was in the Pioneer regiment.
All black and we had white officers and one of the officers, the captain, he resigned because he said he didn't come over for no contraband band. He came over to fight so he resigned.
